items.title: Neural Terrain Classification and Fuzzy Adaptive Covariance Tuning for Improved Outdoor Mobile Robot Localization
items.summary: Abstract Accurate and reliable localization is essential for autonomous outdoor mobile robots operating with low-cost sensors under varying terrain conditions. In such environments, the performance of an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) strongly depends on the appropriate selection of process- and measurement-noise covariance matrices, while fixed covariance parameters often fail to represent terrain-dependent uncertainty. The terrain-specific covariance parameters obtained offline using PSO are incorporated into a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system, which adapts the EKF covariance matrices online according to the estimated terrain type and its associated class-dependent reliability coefficient. The framework was experimentally validated on a wheeled mobile robot using commanded velocity inputs, low-cost Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements, and Real-Time Kinematic Global Navigation Satellite System (RTK-GNSS) reference trajectories collected over multiple outdoor terrain types. Compared with a baseline EKF using fixed covariance matrices, the proposed adaptive approach reduced the average root mean square error by 9.7% and the mean absolute error by 10.2%, with the largest improvements observed on deformable terrains. The results demonstrate that terrain-aware covariance adaptation provides an effective strategy for improving outdoor localization performance using low-cost sensing systems.

items.title: STM32-Based Landmine Detection and GPS Localization Robotic Vehicle
items.summary: Autonomouslandmine detection remains a majorsafety challenge, as conventional manual methods expose personnel to hazardous environments, take considerable time, and may offer limited spatial tracking of detected threats. These limitations are particularly significant in military, humanitarian demining, and hazardous-terrain operations where accurate localization, autonomous navigation, and real-time monitoring are required. This thesis presents an Autonomous GNSS-Guided Mine Detection and Geofenced Monitoring Robot designed to autonomously survey a defined area and identify and spatially record potential metallic mine locations. The system provides dedicated access for field operators and administrators, where operators monitor robot movement, detected targets, and surveyed regions while administrators manage operational data, geofencing, and monitoring functions. The core mechanism combines GNSS positioning with centimeter-level correction, geofencing, barometric sensing, metal detection, and motor control to continuously calculate robot position and constrain movement within the predefined boundary, providing transparent rule-based navigation rather than relying on a black-box navigation model. Supporting features include autonomous movement, virtual fencing, boundary violation prevention, metal-detection marking, real-time position tracking, sensor-status monitoring, location logging, historical data visualization, and remote dashboard monitoring.

items.title: Search and Rescue in Tunnels, an Integrated Approach Using Robotic Platforms
items.summary: Abstract Underground infrastructure such as road and railway tunnels requires reliable communication, localisation, and situational awareness, particularly during search and rescue operations. This article summarises developments carried out within the A‑IQ Ready project in three closely related areas: underground wireless communication modeling, survivor detection, and robotic localisation. A tunnel-specific wireless simulation platform was developed and validated against measurements acquired at the underground facility Zentrum am Berg, enabling realistic prediction of quality-of-service metrics and supporting AI-based communication assessment. Measurement campaigns with a robotic platform were used to generate datasets and calibrate simulation models. For the detection of tunnel users or survivors, a multimodal thermal-LiDAR perception pipeline was implemented on the SPIDER unmanned ground vehicle (UGV). In parallel, LiDAR-based SLAM approaches were investigated for GNSS-denied tunnel environments, resulting in a centralised multi-robot mapping architecture based on LIO-SAM and map-merging concepts. Demonstrations at Zentrum am Berg confirmed the suitability of the developed technologies for search and rescue applications in complex underground infrastructure. They constitute key constituents of enhanced robotic assistance in underground emergency cases.

items.title: Closing Hormuz Without Closing It: Operational Openness and Risk-Mediated Sovereignty
items.summary: Debate about the Strait of Hormuz usually asks whether Iran can close it, how long a military blockade could last, and how far oil prices would rise. This framing treats closure as a visible physical event and openness as its simple absence. The 2026 disruption exposed the limits of that binary. Commercial passage can collapse even when a navigable channel remains and no actor maintains a complete naval barrier. Insurance may be withdrawn or repriced beyond commercial tolerance, satellite navigation and vessel identification may become unreliable, sanctions and port rules may make a lawful voyage unusable, and seafarers may be unable or unwilling to enter a warlike area. This viewpoint introduces the concept of operational openness, defined as the practical capacity to complete safe, lawful, insurable, informationally reliable, and adequately crewed transit. It also proposes \emph{risk-mediated sovereignty} to describe authority exercised by shaping the conditions under which others decide that passage is possible. At Hormuz, this authority is distributed across coastal states, naval forces, insurers, reinsurers, shipping firms, data providers, ports, regulators, and maritime labour institutions. items.title: Aerodynamic Optimization of Freight Trains. Part 1: Characterization of real-world operation from a full-scale measurement campaign
items.summary: The DLR FR8-LAB, a self-contained measurement-system equipped container has been used to take aerodynamic measurements on operational freight-trains. Transient pressure was measured with 330 sensors, and the global transient-forces and moments have been derived: aerodynamic drag – important for operational efficiency, and side-force and rolling moment – important for safety (the risk of overturning and derailment). LiDAR sensors, satellite navigation and thermal cameras are used to couple the aerodynamic measurements with the operating scenarios. Results have indicated significant differences in aerodynamic characteristics based on the operating conditions of freight trains: loading configuration, tunnels, crosswind – that have a significant impact on operating efficiency, and potentially the safety of operation. Together with wind-tunnel experiments performed in parallel – validated by this real-world data – recommendations for aerodynamic optimization can be made for freight-train and infrastructure operators and manufacturers.

items.title: Secure Satellite Communications Using Machine Learning
items.summary: Satellite communication is an important technology for providing communication services over large geographical areas and for transmitting sensitive military, navigational, commercial, and other critical data. With the growth of 6G, IoT, and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, secure satellite communication has become increasingly important. However, wireless and broadcast characteristics expose satellite networks to eavesdropping, spoofing, jamming, signal interference, and intrusion attacks. This paper presents an AI-driven security framework based on Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Federated Learning. One-Class SVM and Sparse Autoencoder are considered for physical-layer authentication; LSTM/RNN models are used for telemetry anomaly and intrusion detection; CNN/CNN-LSTM models are used for jamming detection; RL is used for adaptive beamforming and artificial-noise power allocation; and Federated Learning supports privacy-preserving collaborative training. The proposed architecture integrates these modules to provide adaptive satellite-security capabilities. The stated performance values are project targets and require experimental validation.

Their integration into contemporary armed conflicts has heightened the vulnerability of civilian populations to the direct and indirect consequences of attacks against space-based systems. items.title: Space communications technologies, protocols, and constellations
items.summary: Space communications have evolved from isolated, mission-specific links into interconnected constellation-based networks that underpin critical global infrastructure for navigation, Earth observation, broadband connectivity, scientific exploration, and emergency response. This chapter establishes the technical foundations of these systems, covering end-to-end architecture, communication technologies, protocols, and operational frameworks across the space, ground, and user segments. It analyzes the four principal orbital regimes—low (LEO), medium (MEO), geostationary (GEO), and highly elliptical (HEO)—and their consequences for coverage, latency, link budgets, and constellation design. Radio-frequency and free-space optical communication subsystems are examined alongside inter-satellite links (ISLs), Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) standards, the delay-tolerant networking (DTN) bundle protocol, and the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) non-terrestrial network (NTN) framework. The chapter follows the end-to-end data flow from onboard sensing through ground processing and distribution, then surveys mission operations including launch, commissioning, routine control, anomaly response, constellation coordination, and deorbiting. By consolidating this technical foundation, the chapter prepares the reader for subsequent discussion of resilience, intelligent network management, cybersecurity, and governance in next-generation space communication networks

items.summary: Searching for places using spatial information is useful in a variety of domains that are grounded in the physical world, including urban planning, civil engineering, travel, and many others. Use cases include region recommendation in urban planning, scene recognition in military and defense applications, and Point of Interest recommendation in the travel domain. These spatial search applications are not well-served by modern search engines and Global Navigation Satellite System-based mapping applications for a variety of reasons. Many spatial search questions are naturally specified using a visual query pattern capturing objects of interest and constraints between them, which requires a specialized interface that is not compatible with text-based search engines. Such cases also require a computationally expensive form of search, spatial pattern matching, to resolve. Further, the types of spatial relationships that can be used for spatial search are heterogeneous in nature, including concepts like distance, directionality, topology, and cyclic order, making it difficult to reason over them consistently. For some spatial relationships, searchable data is sparse, with pairwise relationships requiring expensive polygonal data to compute, before search can even begin. items.title: Localize Anywhere Through Adaptive V2X Cooperative Localization for Robust and Precise Urban positioning
items.summary: Accurate and robust localization remains a critical challenge for autonomous vehicles (AVs) operating at dense urban intersections, where Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements are severely degraded by multipath effects and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) conditions. This paper proposes a Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) cooperative localization (CL) pipeline based on the late fusion of 3D bounding boxes (3D BBoxes) observations detected by roadside infrastructure, the ego vehicle, and a partner vehicle. Detected dynamic objects, namely cars, pedestrians, and cyclists, are exploited as shared landmarks following multi-source association and Weighted Box Fusion (WBF). The resulting cooperative measurement is integrated with the degraded GNSS observations in a stackedmeasurement Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). items.title: Onboard-navigation-aided federated fusion for telemetry tracking of high-dynamic flight-test targets
items.summary: Accurate guidance information is essential for telemetry antennas to maintain stable target tracking during flight tests. When the onboard navigation solution degrades or ground-based external tracking measurements are interrupted or abnormal, antenna pointing errors may increase and the telemetry link may become unstable. To improve the reliability of telemetry tracking, this paper applies adaptive federated filtering to a telemetry fusion tracking problem based on onboard navigation and ground-based external measurements. The downlinked SINS/GNSS integrated navigation solution is used as the reference solution at the ground station, and a reference-error state model is established. Ground-based radar measurements and optical measurements are then used to estimate and correct the position and velocity errors of the reference solution. The corrected target state is further converted into azimuth and elevation guidance angles for the telemetry antenna. In the adaptive fusion process, innovation-based fading factors and information allocation coefficients are used to adjust the reliability of different measurement branches and reduce the influence of abnormal measurements. Simulation results under representative disturbance scenarios verify the feasibility of the proposed method and indicate that the corrected target state can provide a more stable guidance reference for telemetry antenna tracking.

items.title: Rapid earthquake magnitude estimation from fuzzy C-means clustering-weighted fusion of seismogeodetic PGD and PGV
items.summary: Rapid and reliable earthquake magnitude estimation is essential for earthquake early warning and tsunami-impact assessment, particularly for large events for which conventional seismic estimates may saturate. This study develops a seismogeodetic magnitude-estimation framework that combines peak ground displacement (PGD) and peak ground velocity (PGV) derived from near-colocated GNSS and strong-motion observations. Fuzzy C-means clustering is used to construct observation-dependent prior weights, while robust and geometry-aware weighting are introduced to reduce the effects of anomalous observations and uneven station distributions. The method was evaluated using 1,147 paired observations from 19 earthquakes with moment magnitudes ranging from 6.1 to 9.0. In leave-one-earthquake-out validation, the PGD-only and PGV-only solutions yield mean absolute errors of 0.338 and 0.320 Mw, respectively, whereas joint PGD/PGV estimation reduces the error to 0.261 Mw. The full robust geometry-aware solution yields an MAE of 0.259 Mw. A two-event holdout test gives a fused mean absolute error of 0.194 Mw, although fusion does not outperform the better single-parameter estimate for every event. These results demonstrate that combining PGD and PGV provides the main improvement in magnitude estimation, while robust and geometry-aware weighting offer additional event-dependent benefits.

items.title: AGGO: Concept and realization of a geodetic observatory in South-America
items.summary: Geodetic observatories form the backbone of global geodetic reference frames. This article reviews the definition of the global geodetic reference system in terms of its origin, orientation, and scale, and its realization through reference frames. At geodetic observatories, reference points are materialized by instruments and survey markers. To achieve the highest possible accuracy, complementary measurement techniques are employed, often operating near the limits of what is technically feasible. Accordingly, a geodetic observatory brings together complex instruments, including a radio telescope for very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), a satellite laser ranging (SLR) system, receiving stations for global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), atomic clocks, absolute and superconducting gravimeters, and complementary sensors. The spatial relationships between the reference points of these instruments are determined through precise local surveys (local ties). The current instrumentation of the Argentine-German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO) is described as an example of the range of measurement techniques needed to establish and maintain a reference site within the global geodetic reference frame. Measurement data collected at AGGO are made freely available through international services.

items.title: A Recursive Bayesian Overbounding Filter Using Gaussian-Pareto Distributions

This estimator leverages Gaussian–Pareto distributions and the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality to provide conservative overbounds for sensor noise constructed from finite data. To enable efficient propagation of Gaussian–Pareto distributions, we develop a method that employs Gaussian mixture models to conservatively approximate these distributions. Given that convolutions with Gaussian mixtures can result in exponential growth of the mixture terms, we devise a culling algorithm that periodically prunes the Gaussian mixture while ensuring conservative overbounding. We assess the performance of the recursive algorithm using a linear, one-dimensional PNT problem. Simulation results consistently demonstrate that the protection levels computed using the proposed algorithm are smaller than those obtained through the traditional Gaussian overbounding method. These results highlight the potential of the proposed estimator to improve PNT system availability in safety-critical applications.
